sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Commercial Shipbuilding of Deep-Sea Dry Cargo and Container Vessels

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law with substantial EU-derived statutory overlay
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: BLEU (Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union) bilateral investment treaties in force with over 90 jurisdictions, including China, India, South Africa and the United States (via OECD framework)
Treaty of Friendship, Establishment and Navigation with the United States (1962) as supplemented by OECD investment instruments
Luxembourg-Germany DTA (2012), Luxembourg-France DTA (1959 as amended), Luxembourg-US DTA (1996), Luxembourg-Netherlands DTA (2015)
EU bilateral and multilateral free trade agreements applicable directly in Luxembourg

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Luxembourg Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs - RBE); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 6 February 2019 implementing the RBE; Law of 10 August 2015 on the Commercial Register; CSSF Circular 18/698.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (public access to the Luxembourg RBE suspended since the Constitutional Court ruling of 16 July 2020; access is granted to competent authorities, notaries, lawyers, accountants, auditors and other obliged entities upon demonstrated legitimate interest)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing of each non-resident corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or commercial court of the shareholder's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Luxembourg is party to the Hague Apostille Convention of 5 October 1961)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Individual UBO identification form and certified passport copies of all ultimate beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issuance authority of the UBO's country of nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization for non-Hague signatory states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and negative solvency certificate issued to the Luxembourg notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed credit institution holding the shareholder's account

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney to local Luxembourg signatory and incorporation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the principal's territory of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn FDI and sectoral authorization declarations for shipbuilding activities under the Law of 19 July 2023
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of the Economy / General Inspectorate of Finance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic certification by Luxembourg authorities, notarized

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors and shareholders against the CSSF consolidated AML/CFT lists, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, the UN Consolidated List, and the OFAC SDN List; enhanced due diligence mandatory where any individual is identified as a Politically Exposed Person or a sanction target, with findings documented in a written KYC file maintained for at least five years after the business relationship ends.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) operating the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), filed electronically through MyGuichet.lu (https://www.lbr.lu and https://registration-rbe.guichet.lu)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be composed of Latin alphabet letters; French is the official registration language, with German or English versions accepted subject to a certified French translation; the name must be preceded or followed by the words Societe a Responsabilite Limitee or the abbreviation SARL; the name must be distinguishable and not misleading as to corporate form or activity.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Etat / Etat luxembourgeois / Luxembourg Government / Sovereign
Luxembourg Financial Centre / Bourse de Luxembourg where it falsely implies public concession
Chambre de Commerce Chamber of Commerce where not licensed
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Luxembourg does not operate a formal administrative name reservation system; the name is checked for availability and distinctiveness at the notarial deed drafting stage and subsequently at RCS filing. Upon rejection, the notary may lodge a rectified deed within the standard length of the incorporation procedure; an administrative appeal lies before the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement) under the amended Law of 19 December 2002, which must be filed within three months of notification of the registry refusal. A rejected name can also be replaced by filing an amended incorporation act with the same notary before registration is completed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Restricted; a licensed registered office provider can serve as the statutory seat, but for ISIC 3011 shipbuilding operations the undertaking must maintain a demonstrable physical industrial presence within Luxembourg, including engineering office, project management facilities and proposed yard or subcontracting premises. A purely virtual office is presumptively inconsistent with commercial substance requirements and would trigger enhanced tax substance scrutiny.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-elevated (estimated 35-40% probability within the first operating year) of unannounced physical inspections by the Ministry of the Economy in relation to the industrial license under the Law of 19 July 2023, the Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA for VAT control, and the Economic Security Authority for FDI vetting of shipbuilding activities.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Luxembourg notary public fee for drafting and solemnizing the SARL incorporation deed
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under the amended Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies (Art. 510-1 et seq.) and notarial fee schedule; approximately USD 1,200-1,800

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registry filing fee for insertion into the Registre de Commerce et des Societes (RCS)
Publication of incorporation act in the Recueil electronique des societes et associations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official per-page publication tariff, circa USD 50-60

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certificate of no bankruptcy / absence of insolvency proceedings (Certificat de non-faillite) for the proposed managers and shareholders
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe et Registre du Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille and consular legalization of foreign shareholder and UBO documents (estimated 5 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs or competent consular post of the document's country of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-document apostille and translation certification market rate, circa USD 70-110 per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified French/German translation of incorporation supporting documents, name clearance dossier and UBO declarations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed sworn translator or notary-appointed translator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per-page rate plus notarial attestation of translation fidelity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation legal due diligence and KYC/AML advisory fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External Luxembourg law firm / AML/CFT compliance advisor
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark hourly rate for senior corporate counsel, estimated 10-15 hours at USD 250-380 per hour

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and commercial substance service agreement (first year)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed domiciliation agent / professional services firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market standard annual fee for regulated domiciliation with substance support, circa USD 1,800-2,400

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP and sanctions screening software subscription and UBO verification checks for all defined individuals
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Approved screening service provider / CSSF-registered data vendor
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate for per-subject screening packages and ongoing monitoring, circa USD 15-25 per subject plus annual platform fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Minimum statutory share capital to be blocked on escrow account before notarial deed (memo item, refundable to company treasury after registration)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Escrow bank or notary blocked account (deposit, not a public fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory minimum capital requirement under amended Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, Art. 510-1 (EUR 12,394.68)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales (Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as consolidated by the Law of 23 July 2016), Articles 710-1 to 710-25 governing the Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL); supplemented by the Grand-Ducal Regulations on the Register of Commerce and on the publication of company acts.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), 1-3 Boulevard Royal, L-2449 Luxembourg.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte constitutif (Articles of Association/Statuts) executed by notarial deed or by private writing with authenticated signatures, filed with the RCS and published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Statutory minimum capital EUR 12,000 (Article 710-5). At incorporation the capital must be fully subscribed; at least 25% of the nominal value of each cash share must be deposited in a blocked escrow account (compte bloqué) with a Luxembourg credit institution and remain blocked until registration, as evidenced by the bank's attestation de blocage. The unpaid balance of cash contributions must be fully liberated within five (5) years. In-kind contributions must be fully paid up immediately.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED by the subscribing founders of [LU SARL] as follows: (1) The full share capital of EUR 12,000 is hereby subscribed; each cash share is paid up to at least twenty-five per cent of nominal value in a blocked escrow account with a Luxembourg credit institution; (2) The registered office is fixed at [address], Luxembourg; (3) [Name] is appointed first manager (gérant) with sole signature power; (4) the manager is authorized to complete all RCS and RESA filings, obtain the business establishment permit, and register the company for VAT and social security.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Capital Escrow Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RCS online portal (www.lbr.lu) and an approved Luxembourg credit institution for the blocked escrow account.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File up to three corporate name reservation requests via the LBR online platform. Upon approval, instruct the founding members to open a blocked escrow account (compte bloqué) with a Luxembourg credit institution and deposit the minimum paid-in tranche of EUR 3,000 (25% of EUR 12,000) or a higher agreed amount, in the name of the future company. Obtain the bank's attestation de blocage stating the future company name, the depositors, and the deposited amount, together with the bank's undertaking to release funds only upon presentation of the RCS registration certificate. Simultaneously collect certified copies of founding members' and managers' identity documents for subsequent notarization.
required_dossiers: Name reservation receipt (certificat de réservation de dénomination)
Bank blocked-account attestation (attestation de blocage)
Draft statutes (projet de statuts)
Certified copies of passports/national identity cards of all founders and proposed managers
Proof of address of each founder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is refused for identity or confusing similarity with an existing registered name, file alternative name reservations within one business day until acceptance. Should the bank request further KYC documentation, supply updated director and shareholder identification within five business days to unblock the escrow certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public registered with the Chambre des Notaires du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg; alternatively a private deed bearing authenticated signatures of all members.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Luxembourg notary (recommended) and present the draft statutes and the attestation de blocage. The constitutive act must contain: the company name, the registered office located in a Luxembourg commune, the company object covering construction and repair of deep-sea dry-cargo and container vessels (ISIC 3011), the share capital of EUR 12,000, the number and class of shares, the identity of the subscribing founders, the appointment of the first gérant, and the duration of the company. Verify the bank certificate is dated no earlier than a few days before execution; execute the deed after confirming subscription and payment declarations.
required_dossiers: Final approved draft of Articles of Association (statuts)
Bank attestation de blocage
Declaration of subscription and payment (déclaration de souscription et de libération)
Identity documents and signature specimens of all founders
Written acceptance statement of the appointed manager (gérant)
If applicable, consent of the réviseur d'entreprises (auditor)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Should the notary or the RCS pre-review identify defective clauses (e.g., unlawful object, missing minimum capital statement, or irregular appointment), execute a corrective rider or amendatory deed (acte rectificatif) within ten business days prior to notarization and re-present the dossier.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), 1-3 Boulevard Royal, L-2449 Luxembourg.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic registration application via the LBR e-forms portal or file the paper dossier at the RCS counter. Pay the EUR 75 registration fee. Attach the executed constitutive act, the bank's attestation de blocage, the manager's acceptance and identity documents, and the criminal record extracts. The RCS verifies statutory compliance, assigns the Luxembourg business registration number (L-number), and delivers the certificate of registration.
required_dossiers: Execution copy of the notarial deed or authenticated private writing
Bank attestation de blocage (original for release certification)
Filled RCS registration application form
Identity documents and criminal record extracts (casier judiciaire) of each manager
Written declaration of acceptance of office by the manager
Proof of payment of the registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query (bulletin de renseignements), respond with the requested evidence (e.g., certified translations of foreign signatures or an updated bank release certificate) within fifteen calendar days. If the registration is refused, remedy by filing a formal corrective instruction or, where necessary, applying to the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg for an order to register.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Justice – Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA), administered through Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon receipt of the RCS certificate, request the RESA publication through the LBR portal for RCS acts. Pay the EUR 19 publication fee. The RESA publishes the incorporation extract containing the statutes, the registered office, the share capital, and the identity of the managers, thereby creating legal opposability of the company's incorporation against third parties.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate and assigned L-number
Electronic copy of the constitutive act for publication
Proof of payment of the RESA publication fee
Manager appointment extract for the published notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RESA publication is suspended due to incomplete RCS data or payment failure, cure by filing an amended extract with the RCS and re-paying the publication fee; the RCS will re-transmit the complete dossier for publication within three business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Establishment Permit, VAT and Social Security Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy – Direction Générale de l'Industrie (autorisation d'établissement); Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AED) for value-added tax; Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS) for social security.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After legal formation, apply online via guichet.lu or at the Ministry of the Economy for the industrial establishment permit (autorisation d'établissement) evidencing the professional qualification and good repute of the manager for the shipbuilding activity. Submit the VAT registration form (formulaire d'immatriculation à la TVA) to the AED. Register the company and all founding/employed personnel as an employer with the CCSS to obtain the social security affiliation number.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate and final statutes
Application for autorisation d'établissement with professional qualification proofs (engineering or nautical/shipbuilding diplomas, prior experience certificates)
Criminal record extracts of the manager from Luxembourg and country of origin
Identity documents of the manager and staff
Lease or ownership title for the shipyard premises with fire safety clearance
VAT registration form (AED)
Employer registration file (CCSS declaration d'affiliation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the autorisation d'établissement is challenged for insufficient professional qualification or missing criminal-record certificate, submit an equivalency recognition request to the Ministry of the Economy and supplement the dossier within one month; any final refusal may be appealed to the Administrative Tribunal (Tribunal administratif) within three months.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – Direction Générale de l'Industrie, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, in conjunction with the commune (municipal administration) where the shipyard is located for classified establishment permitting.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (industrial establishment permit) and Autorisation d'établissement classé (classified establishment operating permit) issued under the Law of 19 July 1996 on classified establishments, as amended, and the Law of 2 September 2011 regulating access to the professions of craftsman, merchant and industrialist.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement, Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development (Le Gouvernement du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category: Class 1 (1ère classe) classified establishment – full EIA report (étude d'incidences sur l'environnement) required prior to authorization, pursuant to the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment and the amended Law of 19 July 1996 on classified establishments; a public inquiry and technical review by the Administration de l'environnement are mandatory for large industrial shipyards.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with EU Industrial Emissions Directive 2010/75/EU (BAT-based emission limit values, including COD ≤ 125 mg/L, TSS ≤ 45 mg/L, oil and grease ≤ 10–30 mg/L in process wastewater); individual water discharge permit under the Law of 19 December 2008 on water management aligned with the Water Framework Directive 2000/60/EC; VOC abatement for coating and painting operations per applicable solvent-emissions regulations (transposing Directive 2010/75/EU, Chapter V) with solvent consumption limits and reduction schemes; hazardous waste (anti-fouling paints, abrasive blasting residues, oily sludge) managed under the Law of 21 March 2017 on waste management and the EU Waste Framework Directive 2008/98/EC; noise and dust control thresholds per environmental permit conditions.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification and rescue-access approval from the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS); structural and building-load inspections and building permit (autorisation de bâtir) from the municipal administration; workplace health and safety clearance from the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM), including crane and lifting equipment verification, electrical safety, confined-space protocols, and occupational health surveillance for shipyard workers.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) for income taxes; Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties; central business portal: guichet.lu and MyGuichet.Lu
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a non-resident enterprise, obtain a Luxembourg business registration number (matricule) via Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) filing service through guichet.lu, then apply for VAT registration with AEDT. Submit: RCS extract, statutes (articles of association), list of managers, power of attorney, identity documents of directors, and proof of EU establishment if applicable. Non-EU entities must appoint an approved VAT representative. The AEDT issues a TVA identification number (LU + 8 digits) typically within 10-15 business days upon complete documentation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; SARL is a fully taxable corporate entity (opaque) resident in Luxembourg subject to: corporate income tax (IRC), municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal, ICC), and net wealth tax. Territoriality: worldwide profits as a resident entity, mitigated by participation exemption regime on qualifying shareholdings; no sub-national corporate income tax divergences (Unitary_National).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not allow check-the-box classification elections for SARLs. Available fiscal mechanisms: VAT group election for Luxembourg resident affiliates (article 63 VAT law); joint taxation regime for fully-owning corporate groups under article 164bis IRC (option for integration); and ordinary participation exemption election where statutory requirements are met. Hybrid mismatch rules under ATAD/EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive are directly applicable, limiting USD/LU double-dip structures.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No registration threshold for non-resident taxable persons making supplies in Luxembourg; domestic small-business exemption applies to entities with annual turnover below EUR 30,000 (but a shipyard commercial entity will exceed this, and exports are generally taxable but zero-rated).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No currently active real-time fiscal clearance or mandatory e-invoicing/digital stamping for B2B or B2G invoices. E-invoicing is permitted; Luxembourg is implementing mandatory B2B B2G e-invoicing through PEPPOL BIS 3.0 from 2026 (B2G already mandatory from 2024). No API-based clearance requirement exists as of the current stage.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of container vessels from Luxembourg to non-EU destinations or shipments to customer within Luxembourg that are then physically transported outside the EU qualify for 0% VAT under Luxembourg VAT law (article 53 VAT law), provided the seller retains proof of export. Related offshore services (e.g., design, engineering, ship management) supplied to non-EU commercial customers may be zero-rated if the foreign business recipient holds a valid foreign VAT ID or adequate documented proof of non-EU status. Bunkering and international transport services are zero-rated under articles 55-57.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (electronic via Luxembourg Customs & Excise, ECS/ICS system)
Bill of Lading or International Air/Sea Waybill
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT payment proof
Delivery or handover certificate signed by the non-EU buyer
Shipyard build contract and end-user/ultimate destination certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg VAT authorities audit export zero-rating strictly. Missing or falsified export evidence leads to retrospective VAT assessment at 17%, punitive interest (0.8% per month, compounded for 6 months per calendar quarter), and fines up to 100% of the tax evaded (article 515/518 LOI). For intentional fraud or abusive passport under EU Anti-Fraud Office (OLAF) coordination, criminal sanctions include imprisonment (up to 5 years) and confiscation. The clawback period is generally 5 years (10 years in case of fraud). Repatriation of foreign currency proceeds beyond 180 days without adequate commercial or force-majeure justification triggers transfer-pricing adjustments, which may result in deemed distribution taxes and additional withholding taxes, but no separate FX-specific statutory fine.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), operating within the Eurosystem and the European System of Central Banks; prudential banking supervision is exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) and, in macroprudential matters, the European Central Bank (ECB).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full and unrestricted convertibility of the euro (EUR) on both current and capital account. Luxembourg applies no exchange-control licensing, no capital-import authorization, and no profit-remittance hurdle; free movement of capital is guaranteed by Articles 63-66 TFEU, EU Directive 88/361/EEC, and the OECD Code of Liberalisation of Capital Movements. Dividend distributions and shareholder-loan repayments may flow freely to EU and non-EU residents subject only to (i) UN/EU/OFAC sanctions and asset-freeze screening, (ii) CSSF anti-money-laundering and customer-due-diligence verification of the underlying transaction, (iii) BCL balance-of-payments statistical reporting for external transactions, and (iv) the Luxembourg company-law distributability test requiring the SARL to prove positive statutory net assets before any dividend outflow.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio apply. Luxembourg does not oblige exporters to repatriate foreign currency within any timeline, nor to convert export receipts into euros; shipbuilding and deep-sea vessel export proceeds may be retained indefinitely in USD or any other freely convertible currency in resident or non-resident foreign-currency accounts. The only binding obligation is statistical: resident entities must report each external transaction equal to or exceeding EUR 12,500 to the BCL via the relationship bank (or directly where the bank is not intermediary), using the harmonized external-transactions coding for goods exports and identifying the underlying commercial invoice and counterparty.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules_note: Optional field preserved for completeness under the mandatory schema; no conversion obligation exists for EUR or USD export accounts.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational multi-currency Account (EUR/USD) and dedicated contractual Escrow Account for ship-installment collections
Operational Account, import/export documentary collection lines, and standby LC (MT760) issuance for refund guarantees
Operational Account, Capital Escrow Account, and USD correspondent clearing for MT103/MT202 cross-border settlement
Operational Account and Maritime Instalment LC programme (MT700 issuance, MT707 amendments, MT756 reimbursement)
Operational Account, host-to-host cash-pooling, and FX hedging execution line (outright forwards, FX swaps)
Operational Account and documentary trade corridors for EU ship-equipment suppliers
Operational Account and receivables-backed installment financing for staged vessel construction
Escrow Account for Asian ship-owner counterparties, USD/CNY clearing corridors, and non-EU remittance channels

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: LOW for the core treasury mandate; MEDIUM-LOW for ancillary operational liquidity. Luxembourg-authorised Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) and Payment Institutions supervised by the CSSF under PSD2 may lawfully provide low-value EUR disbursements, payroll, tax, and supplier payments, but cannot issue, confirm, or advise documentary letters of credit, cannot hold client funds as escrow, and cannot extend credit, trade finance, or FX hedging products. Offshore non-EEA digital EMIs face an even stricter constraint: CSSF/EBA guidance requires client funds to be booked with a licensed EU credit institution, and correspondent-bank compliance will generally reject payment rails originating from unsupervised digital EMI programmes for maritime instalment flows. Any EMI solution should therefore be confined to non-material operating expenses and must never serve as the transmission rail for instalment LC proceeds or escrow monies.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is the default and, in practice, mandatory for a Medium_Risk_Enhanced industrial SARL with maritime counterparties, LC requirements, and escrow structures. Tier-1 banks will require at least one in-person interview in Luxembourg with the substantive shareholder, managing director, or designated compliance representative before account activation. Remote submission of corporate documents via secured portals is accepted during pre-onboarding, but the bank will hold the live account and any MT760/MT700 capability pending a face-to-face closing meeting or a site visit by the relationship manager. Non-resident directors may alternatively sign through a Luxembourg notary or a sworn legal-attestation process, provided the physical identification step is completed with the bank at a later scheduled date.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) opacity caused by holding-chain layering above the SARL (e.g., non-EEA parent trusts, foundations, or nominee arrangements above the 25% participation threshold).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Excerpt of the Luxembourg Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE); notarised chain-of-ownership chart terminating at natural persons; CSSF-compliant CDD questionnaire; certificate of incorporation and register extract for each intermediate entity; and a professional introduction letter from the Luxembourg authorised statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Source-of-wealth for the SARL's minimum capital (EUR 12,500) and injected working capital is undocumented or originates from an undisclosed non-EEA cash pool.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Six months of bank statements of the contributing shareholder; sale-and-purchase agreement or dividend resolution evidencing legitimate patrimony; personal/corporate tax returns and tax-clearance certificates; and a signed source-of-funds declaration countersigned by the Luxembourg notary executing the capital-increase deed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Sanctions, export-control, or maritime compliance exposure arising from charterers, ship-owners, brokers, or equipment suppliers connected to high-risk jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated sanctions-screening output (EU, UN, OFAC, HMT) for the entire counterparty universe; IMO-number and vessel-ownership due-diligence report; Denied-Persons/ECPL and Dual-Use (EU Regulation 2021/821) screening reports; end-use certificate for hull and propulsion packages; and a maritime-sanctions advisory from Luxembourg external trade counsel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Statutory-license gaps, i.e., the shipyard business lacks a Luxembourg Ministry of Economy industrial-establishment authorisation, environmental permits, or, where construction is outsourced abroad, an intra-EU establishment notification under the Services Directive.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ministerial authorisation or exploitation permit; inspection reports from the Administration de l'environnement; certificate of compliance with ISIC 3011 industrial-installation rules; and operational contracts with executing shipyards evidencing permits at the place of physical works.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Escrow-account and maritime-instalment LC mechanics that could be construed as unlicensed grave-holding or unauthorised client-safekeeping activity outside the bank's licence perimeter.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg legal opinion characterising the arrangement as a non-fiduciary contractual escrow (compte de séquestre) under Luxembourg Civil Code Articles 1954-1956; certified copy of the shipbuilding contract with a milestone schedule compliant with ISO/IACS shipyard practice; and draft LC operations conforming to UCP 600 and ISP 98 within the bank's trade-finance policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Unusual treasury profile where the SARL's maritime-focused payment rails are not matched by visible Luxembourg operational substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RCS extract and published financial statements; updated business plan with cash-flow model of the instalment-escrow-LC cycle; physical office or registered-seat inspection report; payroll and Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS) declaration evidence; and VAT registration certificate confirming Luxembourg establishment.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: (i) inbound equity and shareholder loans are routed from the foreign parent via SWIFT MT103/202 to the SARL's account, with ISO 20022 purpose code INVC / CAPITALCONTRIBUTION and the RCS number embedded in structured remittance information; (ii) for transactions equal to or exceeding EUR 12,500, the credit line must carry the BCL external-transactions code for direct-investment capital contribution so the receiving bank can effect automatic balance-of-payments reporting; (iii) non-EEA injections will be settled only if the initiating bank supplies complete sanctions-screening and AML remittance data in the message; (iv) the Luxembourg notary or réviseur d'entreprises must certify the capital increase and the amended Articles must be filed at the RCS before the bank will release funds for operational disbursement; (v) for third-country USD injections, the advice should name the beneficiary bank and the purpose code in the MT202 cover leg to avoid correspondent-bank holds; (vi) SEPA credit transfers suffice for EEA-sourced EUR contributions up to EUR 100,000 but SWIFT is preferred for capital-increase transparency; a compliance hold of one to two business days applies to first-injection funds pending source-of-wealth reconciliation. No Ministry of Economy or CSSF approval is required because the Luxembourg capital account is fully open.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Root clearing is executed via TARGET2 (T2 RTGS) for EUR legs and via correspondent-bank CHIPS/Fedwire for USD legs, with payment initiation through the bank's host-to-host channel: (i) supplier prepayments and local disbursements are sent as SWIFT MT103 referencing the commercial invoice and the BCL external-transactions code; (ii) maritime instalment collections from international ship-owners are documented under buyer-issued instalment LCs (MT700/MT707 sequence), credited directly to the dedicated escrow sub-account; (iii) pay-away to executing shipyards is made by MT103 or, where contract security requires, by confirmed commercial LC governed by UCP 600 with MT756 reimbursement to the advising bank; (iv) refund guarantees and advance-payment bonds are issued as MT760 standby LCs to the buyer's bank; (v) all outbound disbursements above EUR 12,500 are captured by BCL external-statistics reporting through the relationship bank; (vi) each beneficiary is pre-screened against UN/EU/OFAC sanctions and denied-party lists before release, and standing FX-execution instructions are used for cross-currency disbursements to eliminate settlement risk.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD and EUR/GBP outright FX forwards (1-24 month tenors), rollable against the shipbuilding instalment milestone schedule.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in EUR/CNY, EUR/INR, or EUR/other restricted emerging-market pairs where settlement-market convertibility is absent; NDFs are used solely for hedging the SARL's contractual exposure and are subject to EMIR reporting where the non-financial counterparty clearing threshold is exceeded.
FX swaps in EUR/USD and EUR/CNY to optimise daily liquidity between the EUR operational account and USD-denominated instalment receipts.
Cross-currency interest-rate and principal swaps matching long-dated (2-5 year) USD instalment receivables against EUR construction costs.
Plain-vanilla purchased European FX options (premium-paid, no mark-to-market margin calls) to cap adverse EUR/USD moves on the final delivery instalment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual general meeting (assemblée générale ordinaire) approving the annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: None - internal corporate act recorded in the statutory minute book at the registered office; no external filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the financial year end (by 30 June for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct monetary penalty; shareholders may petition the commercial court to order convocation; managers face civil liability for damages

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (financial statements) filing with the RCS and publication in RESA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) managed by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month of approval by the general meeting and, in all cases, within 7 months after the financial year end (by 31 July for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal reminder from the RCS; on the public prosecutor's initiative, criminal fine of EUR 500 to EUR 20,000; failure for 3 consecutive financial years triggers administrative strike-off after formal notice; managers remain jointly and severally liable

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory audit report of the réviseur d'entreprises agréé attached to the annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Filed together with the annual accounts with the RCS and published in RESA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as the annual accounts: within 7 months after the financial year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The RCS refuses to accept the accounts filing without the audit report; criminal fine and professional liability of the auditor in case of knowingly false certification

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owners (UBO confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) operated by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Once per calendar year, within 1 month after the anniversary of the initial RBE registration date (not aligned to the financial year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to EUR 10,000 for late or non-filing; criminal fine up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment for wilful false declarations; blocking of further LBR filings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Luxembourg Business Registers access contribution (cotisation LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due annually upon issuance of the LBR invoice (typically on the registration anniversary); payable within 30 days of invoice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory late-payment interest; suspension of RCS/RBE e-filing access; forced debt collection proceedings

stage_6.entry_description: Identification of the taxpayer: RCS number, legal form (SARL), registered office, business activity code (ISIC 3011) and Luxembourg tax number (numéro d'identification).
stage_6.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident taxpayers filing for a Luxembourg permanent establishment (PE) must add the PE's local designation, local tax registration, and fixed-place-of-business details.
